proof_summary: At \(n=51156\), a sieve computation of the relevant prime counts, followed by finite convolution, finds the unique solution \((k,m)=(16,1119)\), with \(\pi(272)=58\) and \(\pi(626640)=51098\). Monotonicity and the prime-count thresholds at \(k=792\) and \(m=1120\) exclude all larger candidates, so this gives a singleton count at a nonexceptional index.
